plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Fragrant blossoms open on bare, dark branches while snow can still linger on the ground. Each flower is a small, cup-shaped bloom with a sweet, spicy scent. Together they turn orchards and shrine gardens into clouds of pink and white, a sign that spring is on its way.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March, with many Japanese orchards at or near their peak in late February
plants.location: Japan (plum groves and gardens across the country)
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms. In Japan, people held plum-viewing parties before cherry-blossom viewing became the favorite spring custom.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding white bells with a small green mark on the inner petals push up through frost, leaf litter and sometimes snow. They form drifts across woodlands, churchyards and cottage gardens. They are among the first flowers many gardeners see each year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January through March, typically peaking in February in the UK and temperate Europe
plants.location: United Kingdom and temperate Europe (woodlands, parks and gardens)
plants.funFact: Snowdrops flower so early that in recent decades their first blooms in Britain have moved from around the end of February to January.

plants.name: Tabebuia argentea
plants.description: This tree drops its leaves, then covers itself in clusters of bright, trumpet-shaped flowers. When it blooms, whole avenues glow like a golden canopy. Few street trees can match the sight.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January into February, with bloom often continuing through the month
plants.location: Bengaluru (Bangalore), India, along streets and in parks
plants.funFact: The tree sheds its leaves before flowering, so its blooms stand out against bare branches. That timing is why the display looks so dramatic.
